derivation.bandwidth_gb_s: 512 bit bus by 28 Gbps over 8 bits per byte is 1792 GB/s. The whitepaper prints 1792 GB/sec directly.
derivation.fp32: 21760 CUDA cores by 2 FLOP per clock by 2.407 GHz is 104.8 TFLOPS. Whitepaper row 'Peak FP32 TFLOPS (non-Tensor)' is 104.8.
derivation.tf32: Whitepaper row 'Peak TF32 Tensor TFLOPS' is 104.8/209.5, so 104.8 dense.
derivation.fp16_bf16: Whitepaper rows 'Peak FP16/BF16 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' are both 209.5/419, so 209.5 dense. The FP16 accumulate row is 419/838.
derivation.fp8: Whitepaper row 'Peak FP8 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate' is 419/838, so 419 dense.
derivation.fp4: Whitepaper row 'Peak FP4 Tensor TFLOPS with FP32 Accumulate (FP4 AI TOPS)' is 1676/3352. 1676 is dense and 3352 is sparse. The product page headline of 3352 AI TOPS is therefore FP4 with sparsity, exactly twice the dense rate, not four times, and never a valid denominator for a dense measurement.

source: NVIDIA RTX Blackwell GPU Architecture Whitepaper v1.1, Appendix A, Table 3, pages 46 to 47. https://images.nvidia.com/aem-dam/Solutions/geforce/blackwell/nvidia-rtx-blackwell-gpu-architecture.pdf
Same document, page 15 for memory bandwidth and TGP, page 46 for GB202 SM and CUDA core counts
